newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Court rejects Socialist appeal of election verdict.
newsitem.headline: Court rejects Socialist appeal of election verdict.

text.p: A Serbian court rejected on Friday an appeal by President Slobodan Milosevic's Socialist party against a ruling that awarded an election victory to the opposition in the country's second city Nis, an opposition leader said on Friday.

"The court ruled that the Socialist Party's appeal was unfounded," Zoran Zivkovic, the local leader of the opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition, told Reuters by telephone. The Socialists submitted their appeal on Thursday and the court turned it down on Friday, he said, adding he had already received an official notification of the court ruling.

"The entire legal procedure regarding elections in Nis is now over. The only legal venue they still have is to appeal to the Serbian supreme court but this could not delay the transfer of authority in the city," he said.

Mass protests erupted in Serbia after the ruling Socialists annulled opposition election victories in 14 large Serbian towns, including Belgrade, last November on grounds of unspecified "irregularities".
Almost nine weeks of daily Zajedno demonstrations have rattled the foundations of leftist rule in Serbian-led federal Yugoslavia dating back to 1945.
